newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr moves narrowly by Tokyo noon after sharp rise.
newsitem.headline: Dlr moves narrowly by Tokyo noon after sharp rise.

text.p: The dollar was moving extremely narrowly by Tokyo noon on Friday after a dramatic morning climb that briefly took it more than a yen higher than Thursday's New York close. It also rose against the mark.
But talk of heavy sales from 117 yen on up, and a lack of fresh buying factors pushed the greenback back to around 116.60-70 yen, where it spent more than half the morning.

Virtually all the power behind the greenback's climb appeared to come from short-covering, primarily by interbank operators, although there was some unconfirmed talk of bids by investors, mainly life-insurers, at the lows.

"This morning's storm of short-covering can be seen as a natural response to the speed with which the dollar fell overnight," one dealer at a U.S. bank said. The greenback fell as low as 114.70 yen in London trade overnight.
But she added that there was a sense in the market that this recovery could still be fragile and that the strength of the downside has yet to be fully confirmed.
The short-covering, which first emerged in early Tokyo, carried the greenback rapidly up from its day's low of 115.94 yen.

Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's comment that the recent Group of Seven agreement on currencies had filtered through to the market, and that Japan would act in a timely and appropriate manner based on this agreement, may have supported the rise briefly, but had little overall impact, dealers said.
After hitting 117.06 yen, the dollar fell back in the face of sales, which some dealers said were likely to have come from exporters. But others disagreed.

"Exporters are unlikely to come out to sell with any force until the dollar rises somewhat higher," one trust bank dealer said. But the dealer at the U.S. bank said offers appeared to be lined up from 117.00 to 117.50 yen, although they were not necessarily from exporters.

She added that while the greenback now appeared to have carved itself a range of roughly 116.50 to 117.00 yen, there was still the potential for it to break out for strong moves in either direction, should appropriate factors emerge.
"If we took the dollar up to 117 yen by the time Europe comes in, it could rise further overseas," she said.
But trade in general was thin, with many participants sidelined ahead of next week's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).

Uncertainty about whether or not this will result in a U.S. interest rate rise has made the market wary of selling dollars. Some dealers said such a rise would support the dollar, while others said a rise of 25 basis points has already been factored in.
